gloss: He was afraid
notes: Source grammatical qualifications retained: omitted fear object uses transitive construction; expressed object takes -te or -a. Impersonal construction has experiencer as object. Parenthetical boro-e-a is source analysis of boroya, preserved in Notes rather than inserted into lexical Form.
raw_source: <boro>  {v} `to ^fear; to be ^afraid.__When the object of the fear is not expressed, this is used transitively, e.g. <borokeDae:>__"He was afraid", <alom boroya (boro-e-a)>__"Don't be afraid".__When the object of fear is expressed it takes a <-te> or <-a> marker, e.g. <alom borotekowa> or <alom borowakowa>__"Do not be afraid of them".__<Boro> is used in an impersonal construction with the experiencer as object, e.g. <eDka borokiDJa>__"I was thoroughly scared".__It is also sometimes used with a personal subject and a direct personal object with the meaning "to make someone give in (give up) out of fright'.  $01232$
